about: The work of a lift technician

lines.text: Most of us step into a lift every day without thinking about it.
We press a button, the doors close, and we arrive safely at our
floor. This simple journey depend on the work of technicians like Mr Rahim,
lines.note: Agreement: 'this simple journey' is one thing, so it is 'depends'.

lines.text: who has been repair lifts for nearly twenty years. Every month, he checks
lines.note: Verb form: after 'has been' it is 'repairing'.

lines.text: every lift in the estate and climbs into the dark shaft above them.
lines.note: Pronoun: 'every lift' is singular, so it is 'it'.

lines.text: He oils the cables, tests the brakes and replaces any part who looks
lines.note: 'Who' is for people. A part takes 'that' or 'which'.

lines.text: worn. The job is dirty and tiring, and it often continues after dark.
When residents are trapped inside, he must reach them as quick as he can.
lines.note: Word form: 'reach' is a verb, so it takes the adverb 'quickly'.

lines.text: Once, he free a frightened child who had been stuck for an hour.
lines.note: Tense: it happened once in the past, so it is 'freed'.

lines.text: Mr Rahim admits that few people thank him, because he does not mind.
lines.note: Connector: the two ideas contrast, so it is 'but', not 'because'.

lines.text: He says there is no best reward than knowing that thousands of his
neighbours travel up and down safely because of his careful work.
